Hey /v/Warhammer!

I'm kinda interested in starting to play this beautiful game. The biggest issue right now is that I don't really know too much about the armies. I was interested in the Harlequin, the Tau, and the Tyranids. So my question is what army would you guys say would be best to play as? And what are your thoughts on each one?

Hey there, welcome to the hobby! We're a little bit dead now, but I'll do my best.

So the biggest thing in terms of 40k (and Fantasy), is to play an army that looks awesome to you. Most armies favor a certain playstyle, but it's not ironclad.

I'll preface this by saying that there isn't a single best army to play as. It's really up to your taste as flavors of the month come and go.

Tau

  • The Tau are pretty cool. They favor mobile gun platforms and gun-lines. (With the exception of some elite units like the riptide) Individually weak, but when used in concert they're devastating. But don't let anything get into close-combat with you. Their biggest weakness is the psychic phase, since Tau have no warp presence. So, be prepared to twiddle your thumbs as Chaos/Daemon players summon a new unit or two onto the battlefield every turn.

Tyranids

  • Tyranids got revamped a few months ago, and I don't know any 'nid players so my info isn't the best. But, that said, nids are good at overwhelming numbers and monsters. Lots of bodies backed by horrifying creatures. Just be careful since a few of the big-guys are total duds on the 'field.

Harlequinns

  • Harlequins are pretty new, and again I'll be honest and say that I don't know a lot about them. From what I understand they're kind of a glass cannon. However the most important thing about the Harlequins is that they're not a fully fledged army. Sure you can field a force of only Harlequins, but they've only got a handful of units. They've been more or less designed as allies for Eldar and Dark Eldar allies (which are two armies you should look into if you like Harlequins).

Anyways, let me know what you think or if a more experienced player is lurking please feel free to jump in!

You hit it right on the nail. Always consider the look of the Army for your first. This way you don't have to worry about getting bored of the aesthetics later on. I would highly recommend going to a Games Workshop store and talking to the employees. They will definitely help you get a feel for the armies and they might even play a sample game to see if it is really your thing.
